content: I was charged $49.99 twice for the same monthly subscription this morning. My account shows only one active plan, and I need the extra charge reversed because it affects a bill due tomorrow. I have both transaction IDs ready. Can you fix this?

I can't reverse the charge myself because I don't have access to your payment accounts or the merchant's billing system. Here's the fastest way to get it fixed before your bill is due.

## 1. Contact the merchant first (usually fastest)
Duplicate same-day charges are often caught and reversed quickly once reported.
- Use the company's **billing support chat or phone line**, not email. Live channels move faster.
- Say something like:
  > "I was charged $49.99 twice on [date] for one monthly subscription. My account shows one active plan. Transaction IDs: [ID 1] and [ID 2]. Please refund the duplicate charge [ID 2] and confirm the refund reference number."
- Ask for a **refund confirmation number** and an expected timeline.

## 2. Check whether one charge is just a pending authorization
In your bank or card app, see if one of the two is marked **"pending."** Duplicate authorizations often drop off on their own within 1–5 business days and never post. If one is pending, ask your bank whether they can release it early.

## 3. Call your bank or card issuer at the same time
Since the bill is due tomorrow, don't wait on the merchant:
- Report it as a **duplicate charge**. Banks treat this as a straightforward dispute.
- Give them both transaction IDs.
- Ask for a **provisional credit** while they investigate. Many issuers grant this quickly for duplicate charges.

## 4. Protect tomorrow's bill
Refunds can take 3–10 business days to settle even after they're approved, so plan for the money not arriving in time:
- Ask whoever issues tomorrow's bill for a **short extension** or a one-time late-fee waiver. Mention the pending duplicate-charge dispute.
- If it's a bank account, ask about overdraft protection or a temporary courtesy waiver.
- If possible, temporarily move $49.99 from savings or another account to cover the gap.

## 5. Keep records
Screenshot both charges, your account page showing one active plan, and any refund or dispute confirmation numbers. You'll need them if the refund stalls.

If you tell me which service charged you, I can help you find their billing contact or draft a more detailed message.

Wait, why are you telling me to call my bank and the merchant myself? I'm talking to you because I thought you were the support channel for this service. I don't want a guide on how to do your job; I want my money back. If you can't do it, who exactly has the authority to fix this right now?

I'm sorry for the confusion. I should have been clearer: **I'm not this service's support channel.** I'm Claude, a general-purpose AI assistant made by Anthropic. I'm not connected to the company that charged you, I can't see your account or transactions, and I have no ability to issue refunds. Using me doesn't put your request in front of their billing team.

## Who can actually reverse the charge today

**1. The merchant's billing team.** They can refund the duplicate directly, often the same day. Use the "Contact us," "Help," or "Billing" link in your account on their website or app. Choose live chat or phone if they offer it.

**2. Your bank or card issuer.** They can dispute the duplicate and often issue a **provisional credit** quickly, sometimes the same day. Call the number on the back of your card. You don't need the merchant's cooperation for this.

Do both at the same time. Since your bill is due tomorrow, the bank is your best chance at getting money back fast.

## What I can do right now

- **Draft the exact message** for the merchant's support chat or email, using your transaction IDs.
- **Write a short script** for your bank call so it takes five minutes.
- **Help you find the right contact** if you tell me which service charged you.

Which service was it? I'll get the message ready so you can send it immediately.

Wait, what? I thought I was talking to customer support! Why are you telling me you're an AI and not the company? This is incredibly confusing and I don't have time to be bounced around when I have a bill due tomorrow. 

Since you claim you can help me find the right contact, just tell me: who exactly do I need to call to get my $49.99 back right now?

I'm sorry about the confusion. Here's the direct answer:

## Call your bank or card issuer right now

**Use the phone number on the back of the card that was charged.** This is your fastest option with a bill due tomorrow, because the bank can act without waiting on the merchant.

When you get a person, say:

> "I was charged $49.99 twice this morning by [company name] for one subscription. I'd like to dispute the duplicate. The transaction IDs are [ID 1] and [ID 2]. Can you issue a provisional credit today? I have a bill due tomorrow."

Ask them for:
- A **dispute or case number**
- **When the credit will appear** in your account
- Whether they can **waive any overdraft or late fee** if the money doesn't arrive in time

If one of the charges shows as **"pending,"** ask them to release it. It may never post at all.

## Then contact the company that charged you

I can't name them because I don't know which service it was. Look for the company name on the charge in your banking app, or in the receipt email for the subscription. Their billing support is usually under **Help, Support, or Billing** in your account settings. Give them the same two transaction IDs and ask them to refund the duplicate.

## If the refund won't land by tomorrow

Call whoever issued tomorrow's bill and ask for a **one- or two-day extension**. Tell them you have an open duplicate-charge dispute. Most companies will agree to that.

If you tell me the name of the subscription service, I'll tell you exactly where to find their billing contact.
